title: Perfil de salud y tipo de contratación de académicos universitarios durante la pandemia por COVID-19 Health profile and type of employment among university academics during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Introduction: Employment status has been associated with declining health among university faculty, especially in crisis contexts such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Objective: To evaluate the association between employment status and health profile, as well as the risk of COVID-19 infection, among faculty members at the Autonomous University of Tlaxcala during the pandemic. Materials and methods: A descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted between February and April 2022 with a convenience sample of 1,645 faculty members from the Autonomous University of Tlaxcala. A questionnaire, validated by experts, was used to collect sociodemographic and health data, differentiating between employment statuses (full-time vs. Associations between variables were analyzed using chi-square tests and adjusted residuals. A binary logistic regression model was fitted to control for confounding variables. Results: Full-time teachers had a higher frequency of chronic degenerative diseases than part-time teachers. Logistic regression confirmed that employment status was significantly associated with the risk of COVID-19 infection (OR = 0.667, 95% CI: 0.51–0.873, p = 0.0031), after controlling for age, sex, and the presence of chronic degenerative diseases. title: Exploring the Effects of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Parents’ Well-Being: A Comparative Analysis of Pre-, During, and Post-Lockdown
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns heavily impacted the stress levels of families worldwide. We examined parental stress levels regarding a variety of subtopics (including finances, schooling, and seeing extended family) in North Bay, Ontario, Canada. A mixed-method survey approach was used with a volunteer sample of 101 parents from the North Bay community. Included in the survey were 25 potential parental stressors, which parents were asked to rate in terms of their stressfulness, both during the COVID-19 lockdowns and post-pandemic. To accomplish this, participants were administered only one questionnaire, after the height of the pandemic was over, and asked to reflect on both the current time and on the time during the lockdown phase of the pandemic. General stress levels were higher after the lockdowns ended compared to during the lockdowns, indicated by 20 out of the 25 surveyed parental stressors. Four themes were identified in the qualitative data obtained from open-ended questions: ability to parent; requiring additional support; mental and physical well-being; and child-rearing. Specifically, in terms of the first theme, some parents felt that parenting had become more difficult, while others did not. With respect to theme two, many parents felt a need for support in a variety of areas, which relates to theme three, as supports were often desired to improve mental or physical well-being. The fourth theme highlighted the opportunity to spend more time at home with family and raise children according to parents’ own principles. Parents were also asked about changes in their behaviours, like gambling and alcohol use; gambling, in particular, increased during and after the pandemic compared to before. However, parents reported that the difficulty associated with continuing to parent as they did before the lockdowns was minimal, and that it did not change during or after the lockdowns. Finally, parents were asked about changes to their own mental and physical health; results were mixed, but approximately half of participants perceived positive changes in their well-being. Thus, compared to existing research, the current study provides a more comprehensive overview of stressors experienced by families in the wake of COVID-19 lockdowns. It also brings to light suggestions and recommendations from survey respondents to improve parents’ quality of life in post-COVID-19 North Bay, Ontario.

title: Asymmetric Recovery Pathways of Seoul Subway Ridership After the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: This study examines patterns of ridership recovery across Seoul subway stations following the COVID-19 pandemic and identifies the factors associated with recovery stagnation. To this end, we apply cluster analysis, Markov transition analysis, and binary logistic regression using subway ridership data from 2019 to 2025. We classify station-level recovery into four types: Entrenched Low-Recovery, Partial Recovery, Improved Recovery, and Over-Recovery. The results reveal substantial variation in recovery trajectories across stations. Entrenched Low-Recovery stations display strong path dependence and state persistence, whereas Improved Recovery and Over-Recovery stations exhibit lower state stability and higher transition probabilities. In addition, recovery in morning commuting and evening travel, restaurant density, and average sales per store reduce the likelihood of recovery stagnation, whereas stations with stronger transfer functions are more likely to remain in a low-recovery state. These findings indicate that post-pandemic urban rail recovery is not a uniform return to pre-pandemic ridership levels, but a heterogeneous and dynamic process shaped by station functions and surrounding urban conditions. From a policy perspective, this heterogeneity highlights the need for station-specific recovery strategies that account for differences in transportation and local characteristics. More broadly, by revealing the persistence and transitions of station-level recovery states, this study provides a dynamic perspective on post-pandemic urban rail recovery beyond point-in-time comparisons of ridership change.

title: In Silico Variant Analysis Identifies Mutations in TP53 Gene Increasing The Risk of Cancer in COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Introduction: The Coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) disease caused by SARS-CoV-2 emerged as a global pandemic due to its lethal nature and great potential to spread rapidly. It is predicted that the coronavirus infection can leave detrimental consequences in infected patients even after recovery. Therefore considering the ability of the virus to induce lethal mutations in the host genome, we aimed to identify variants in COVID-19 patients irrespective of their origin. Methods: For the present study, transcriptomic data of patients were retrieved from the GEO dataset of the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) (GSE216811 and GSE197976 (India), GSE174786 (Germany), GSE171052 (Canada), GSE 206264 (Spain) and GSE206677 (Japan)). Each dataset was assessed independently for Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). After quality check and removing low-quality reads the samples were normalized using Bcf-tools norms. Further, SnpEff eff and SIFT4g annotator was used to identify and annotate variants occurring in each sample. The common variants occurring in all the patients of COVID-19. Were identified through a Venn diagram. The systems biology approach was used to identify hub genes out of common mutated genes. Results and Discussion: CytoHUBBA plug-in of Cytoscape identified TP53 as the hub gene mutated due to COVID- 19 infection. TP53 is a tumor suppressor gene that plays an important role in DNA damage repair, cell cycle regulation, and inducing apoptosis. Conclusion: Therefore, we conclude that mutation in TP53 causes loss of suppression potential of the gene increasing the risk of cancer in such individuals.

title: Production of multivalent, enveloped virus-like particles (eVLPs) targeting SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and RSV in engineered CHO cells
abstract: Les virus respiratoires tels que le SARS-CoV-2, le virus de la grippe A (IAV) et le virus respiratoire syncytial (RSV) continuent de représenter une charge importante pour la santé mondiale, en particulier chez les populations vulnérables. Les vaccins actuels nécessitent souvent des immunisations répétées et offrent une efficacité limitée, ce qui souligne la nécessité de plateformes de nouvelle génération capables de fournir une protection large et simultanée. Dans ce contexte, les vaccins multivalents basés sur des particules pseudo-virales (VLP) représentent une approche prometteuse en raison de leur capacité à présenter plusieurs antigènes sous une forme particulaire hautement immunogène. Cette thèse explore une nouvelle plateforme de VLP enveloppées (eVLP) dérivées de cellules d’ovaire de hamster chinois (CHO), dans laquelle l’expression de la protéine Spike (S) complète du SARS-CoV-2 suffit à induire la formation de particules (S-VLP). Nous avons évalué si les S-VLP pouvaient servir pour l’incorporation d’antigènes hétérologues en co-exprimant l’hémagglutinine (H1) et la neuraminidase (N1) du virus de la grippe A, ainsi que la protéine de fusion (F) du RSV, afin de générer des eVLP bi- et trivalentes par expression transitoire et stable dans des cellules CHO modifiées exemptes de particules de type rétroviral (RVLP). Les eVLP obtenues ont été produites à des rendements compatibles avec une fabrication à grande échelle et ont présenté des propriétés biochimiques favorables. Chez la souris, elles ont induit de fortes réponses humorales et cellulaires spécifiques des antigènes des trois virus et ont conféré une protection complète contre une infection grippale létale à de faibles doses d’antigène. L’incorporation des antigènes de l’IAV n’a pas compromis l’immunogénicité dirigée contre la protéine S, ce qui soutient la compatibilité de la présentation multivalente d’antigènes au sein d’une même particule. Du point de vue de la fabrication, les cellules CHO déficientes en RVLP constituent une plateforme plus propre et plus sûre pour la production d’eVLP, en réduisant les défis en aval liés à la contamination par des particules endogènes. Dans l’ensemble, ce travail établit les S-VLP dérivées de cellules CHO comme une plateforme flexible et évolutive pour le développement de vaccins multivalents, soutenant leur potentiel pour simplifier le développement de stratégies vaccinales multivalentes contre les principaux virus respiratoires.

title: Abstract No: 395 A Single-Center Retrospective Study on Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of COVID-19 Complicated with AKI
abstract: COVID-19 has been one of the globally pandemic diseases in recent years, and AKI is a common complication. This study aims to compare COVID-19 AKI patients with AKI patients due to other causes during the same period. Through a 12-month follow-up, it seeks to identify the unique clinical characteristics and outcomes of COVID-19 AKI patients, explore renal recovery and survival in COVID-19 complicated with AKI, and analyze risk factors for death within 12 months in COVID-19 patients with AKI.

title: Future Jobs for People with Disabilities Post-COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Technology was the driving force behind future employment for people with disabilities and created opportunities, but it posed challenges regarding the gap between PWD and people without disabilities. Driven largely by the expansion of remote and hybrid work, current employment rates for PWD saw remarkable gains, even outpacing those of nondisabled workers in some sectors. The call of post-pandemic RTO mandates could erode the progress in flexibility of work and technology achieved by PWD in term of progress in the labor market during the pandemic in the United Kingdom and United States. In both countries, the legal framework encourages this kind of flexible working as a potential reasonable accommodation/adjustment, though the United Kingdom had implemented more explicit, universal rights to request it. The second half of the chapter examines the role of AI as a potential to enhance future work opportunities for workers with disabilities in both the United Kingdom and the United States through advanced assistive technologies and flexible work options. However, the realization of this potential could heavily be contingent on proactive policy and regulatory frameworks in each country to address inherent biases in AI-powered hiring tools and government systems. The post-pandemic labor market offered some potential for positive change, largely driven by technological shifts. However, despite the opportunities, the economic situation in many LMICs stayed the same or even worsened. In many of these countries the lack of robust, disability-inclusive policies and social safety nets would make individuals with disabilities vulnerable to economic shocks.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Employment for Persons with Disabilities in the Twenty-First Century Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Prior to the pandemic, both the United Kingdom and United States saw increasing employment rates for people with disabilities, driven by policy shifts, strong economies, and rising self-reporting of disabilities. However, significant employment gaps persisted, and workers with disabilities often faced inequality in pay, opportunities, and workplace accommodations. There was a steady increase in the number of people with disabilities who worked in the United Kingdom between 2013 and 2019. However, the gap between disabled and nondisabled people narrowed, but a substantial disparity remained. Despite improvements, workers with disabilities still faced notable inequalities. They were more likely to be in part-time work and lower-skilled occupations. Prior to the pandemic, employees with disabilities were more likely to face discrimination, leading to lower wages, fewer opportunities for advancement, and a lack of necessary accommodation. Employment for people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States had seen significant shifts in the twenty-first century, particularly shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic. While pre-pandemic efforts showed some progress, the pandemic temporarily reversed trends before accelerating new opportunities, most notably the expansion of remote work. For workers with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), the COVID-19 pandemic amplified preexisting systemic disadvantages. While the pandemic caused widespread job loss, workers with disabilities, who were already disproportionately in the informal sector, suffered more severe economic impacts. Post-pandemic, recovery has been uneven, with some progress seen through remote work, but the employment gap persists.

title: Unraveling the Effects of SARS-CoV-2 on Dementia: A Comprehensive Study
abstract: Since late 2019, a pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2, a highly contagious coronavirus, has jeopardized human and public health. Neurodegeneration and structural brain diseases produce dementia, which is developing rapidly. Strong evidence of COVID-19 brain abnormalities as neurotrophic viruses impair neurological systems. Neuron and glial cell degeneration can affect nerve transmission and brain function. Damage to these brain components raises dementia risk. Multiple studies linked SARS-CoV-2 to dementia. This manuscript contains selective data. This study aims to review the findings and suggest strategies to improve SARS-COVID dementia management. The study makes use of medical research databases like Google Scholar, PubMed, Medline, and Embase. Furthermore, information is also collected by recognized health organizations and government agencies. COVID-19 can produce neuropsychological deficits, agitation, confusion, inattention, and disorientation. Thus, SARS can worsen dementia and neurodegeneration. This article summarizes COVID-19's effects on dementia patients from several sources. The focus on existing treatments for affected patients ties the two.

title: Severe Pediatric Neurological Manifestations with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) Linked to COVID-19 Pandemic: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Introduction: Since December 2019, COVID-19 has caused global health challenges. Among pediatric populations, SARS-CoV-2 infections have led to severe multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), often accompanied by neurological complications. Objective: This study aimed to assess and characterize the neurological manifestations of MIS-C in pediatric patients with COVID-19. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional cohort study was conducted on 303 pediatric patients admitted to a pediatric intensive care unit in Upper Egypt between March 2020 and March 2023. Patients were divided into three groups: Group I (MIS-C, PCR-positive), Group II (MIS-C, serologypositive), and Group III (non-MIS-C, PCR-positive). Neurological symptoms, laboratory markers, and outcomes were analyzed. Results and Discussion: Neurological manifestations were most frequent in Group II (53.5%), followed by Group I (45.0%) and Group III (14.3%). Convulsions, decreased consciousness, headaches, and weakness were significantly more common in Group I. Inflammatory markers (CRP, D-dimer, ferritin, and troponin) were elevated in Groups I and II. Radiological abnormalities were infrequent, and neuroimaging findings showed no significant intergroup differences. Hospital stays were longest for Group I (mean 7.8 days), and mortality was highest in Group I (21.7%). Severe neurological symptoms correlated with adverse outcomes. Conclusion: This study emphasizes the high prevalence of neurological symptoms in pediatric patients with COVID-19-associated MIS-C, especially in those with positive serology. Symptoms like convulsions, decreased consciousness, headaches, and weakness were more common, with severe cases linked to elevated ferritin and D-dimer levels and abnormal neuroimaging findings. It highlights the importance of thorough neurological assessments in these patients and calls for further research into the long-term neurological effects of COVID-19 in children.

source_records.title: Severe Pediatric Neurological Manifestations with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) Linked to COVID-19 Pandemic: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
source_records.abstract: Introduction: Since December 2019, COVID-19 has caused global health challenges. Among pediatric populations, SARS-CoV-2 infections have led to severe multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), often accompanied by neurological complications. Objective: This study aimed to assess and characterize the neurological manifestations of MIS-C in pediatric patients with COVID-19. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional cohort study was conducted on 303 pediatric patients admitted to a pediatric intensive care unit in Upper Egypt between March 2020 and March 2023. Patients were divided into three groups: Group I (MIS-C, PCR-positive), Group II (MIS-C, serologypositive), and Group III (non-MIS-C, PCR-positive). Neurological symptoms, laboratory markers, and outcomes were analyzed. Results and Discussion: Neurological manifestations were most frequent in Group II (53.5%), followed by Group I (45.0%) and Group III (14.3%). Convulsions, decreased consciousness, headaches, and weakness were significantly more common in Group I. Inflammatory markers (CRP, D-dimer, ferritin, and troponin) were elevated in Groups I and II. Radiological abnormalities were infrequent, and neuroimaging findings showed no significant intergroup differences. Hospital stays were longest for Group I (mean 7.8 days), and mortality was highest in Group I (21.7%). Severe neurological symptoms correlated with adverse outcomes. Conclusion: This study emphasizes the high prevalence of neurological symptoms in pediatric patients with COVID-19-associated MIS-C, especially in those with positive serology. Symptoms like convulsions, decreased consciousness, headaches, and weakness were more common, with severe cases linked to elevated ferritin and D-dimer levels and abnormal neuroimaging findings. It highlights the importance of thorough neurological assessments in these patients and calls for further research into the long-term neurological effects of COVID-19 in children.

title: Nasal Vaccine: A Special Prominence on SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Nasal administration of mucosal medications and vaccines is an alternate and promising method of drug and vaccine delivery. Mucosal pathways can be used selectively for various disorders due to many benefits. Many initiatives are now being made to yield effective medications and cutting-edge nasal delivery systems. The structure of the nasal cavity and key features were discussed in this review. With a focus on vaccine distribution, the benefits, successes, and difficulties of using the nasal route for medical purposes were examined. The strong result supports the benefits and security, of the safety of nasal medication and vaccination administration. This alternate path may help many unmet medical needs and may also make big vaccination drives or expensive, protracted chronic therapies possible. Today, despite some lingering criticism, the area of nasal medicine and vaccine delivery is expanding quickly, supported by recent advancements in nanotechnology, imaging, and administration devices. The variety of drugs that have been licensed for nasal delivery is expected to increase significantly.

title: Investigating the Relationship Between Postpartum Depression, Antenatal Depression, Corona Disease Anxiety, and Personality Traits During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Introduction and Aim: Postpartum depression has a profound impact, both physically and psychologically, on both the mother and her newborn. With a focus on the prevalent psychological complications following the onset of this condition, this study aimed to explore the correlation between antenatal depression and Corona disease anxiety, personality traits, and postpartum depression during the COVID-19 pandemic. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional descriptive-analytical study investigated women receiving care at health centers affiliated with Kerman University of Medical Sciences during the last month of their pregnancy and the postpartum period in 2022. Following the acquisition of informed consent, participants were assessed using various measures, including demographic and obstetric information, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, the Corona Disease Anxiety Scale (CDAS), and the NEO Personality Inventory-Revised during their third trimester of pregnancy. The same group of participants completed the Edinburgh Depression Scale and the Corona Disease Anxiety Scale (CDAS) 4-6 weeks after childbirth. Results and Discussion: There was a significant correlation between family income, unwanted pregnancy as perceived by both the mother and father, and antenatal depression. Additionally, marital satisfaction played a significant role in postpartum depression. Furthermore, antenatal depression was significantly associated with neuroticism, agreeableness, and physical symptoms related to Corona disease anxiety. Personality traits, with the exception of extroversion and conscientiousness, and various domains of Corona disease anxiety, excluding psychological symptoms, were also significantly associated with postpartum depression. Conclusion: During pandemics or epidemics, such as the COVID-19 outbreak, experiencing mental distress during pregnancy can contribute to mental health issues during the postpartum period. This risk is particularly true in individuals with unique personality traits, emphasizing the need for increased focus on mental health within prenatal care during these crises.

title: Effects of COVID-19 on Food Supply: A Systematic Review
abstract: Objective: The COVID-19 outbreak has had a significant influence on several critical industries, including agriculture, education, and the economy. This essay investigates these processes, with a focus on agriculture, where the repercussions have been particularly harsh for poor groups dealing with unpredictable food supplies and food safety. Methods: Along with a critical examination of the shift to digital education systems, the report highlights the major obstacles that lie ahead for regions lacking adequate digital infrastructure and digital literacy. There have been notable disruptions in the economy as well. Manufacturing, the financial markets, and tourism have all seen major downturns. Results and Discussion: The study emphasizes the crucial part that following safety measures and boosting immunization campaigns play in mitigating these negative consequences while supporting economic recovery. Also, new technical solutions have emerged throughout this time. The application of drone technology to contactless food delivery is a notable illustration of how creativity can overcome the challenges posed by the pandemic. Conclusion: Finally, the report recommends the development of specific and rigorous methods to strengthen recovery efforts in these critical areas.

title: Alterations in Liver Function Biomarkers Among Moderately Severe COVID‐19 Patients in southeastern Serbia: A Retrospective Single‐Center Study
abstract: Liver biochemical abnormalities have been reported in nearly half of patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Aim of the study was to determine the prevalence of altered liver biomarkers (ALT, AST, LDH, GGT, and albumin) in COVID-19 patients with a moderately severe clinical picture at hospital admission, and to assess the presence of altered liver-related biomarkers in the absence of a severe clinical presentation. Research material consisted of medical histories of patients with moderately severe clinical picture of COVID-19 who were hospitalised at the Clinic for Infectious Diseases of the University Clinical Centre in Niš. The study included 655 patients (425 male and 230 female) that were divided into three groups: patients without comorbidities (NC), patients with arterial hypertension (HTA), and patients previously diagnosed with diabetes mellitus (DM). Additionally, within each research group, patients were divided into three age subgroups: patients aged 20-40 years, 40-60 years, and over 60 years. AST, ALT, and LDH showed statistically significant differences across the defined groups, while GGT did not. Logistic regression confirmed increased odds for elevated AST and LDH values ​​in all older and comorbid groups, with the most pronounced effects for LDH. For ALT, significantly increased odds were observed among patients with HTA (40–60 years) and DM (40–60 years). The most pronounced changes were observed in elderly patients and those with hypertension and diabetes, with LDH emerging as the most sensitive, although non-specific, biomarker, likely reflecting systemic inflammation and disease severity in addition to possible hepatic involvement.

title: Work and non-work concerns and impact on healthcare workers during the COVID-19 first wave in Brunei Darussalam: Identifying key risk groups for targeted support
abstract: Healthcare workers (HCWs) played an integral role as front-line essential workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. They were at high risk of COVID-19 transmission and faced psychological effects of fatigue and burnout, which ultimately influenced their participation and performance during the pandemic. This study was conducted to assess work and non-work concerns and the impact of COVID-19 on HCWs in Brunei Darussalam. A cross-sectional study using a web-based and self-administered questionnaire was conducted from July to August 2020, with 511 HCWs in Brunei Darussalam. Data were analysed for associations between demographic profile and perceived work, non-work concerns, and impact of the outbreak on the HCWs during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic. The risk of acquiring COVID-19 (79.8%) and the risk of transmission to family members (90.8%), friends (88.6%) and colleagues (87.2%) were the primary concerns reported by HCWs. Additionally, 62.8% reported being tasked with additional work duties, 59.2% experienced increased workload, 54.5% experienced feeling stressed, and 45.5% felt the effects of manpower shortages. Multivariate analysis showed higher work concerns among doctors (OR=2.29, CI:1.14-4.61), nurses (OR=2.47, CI:1.37-4.48), and those working in hospitals (OR=3.22, CI:1.54-6.73), health centres/clinics (OR=3.82, CI:1.78-8.18), and the National Isolation Centre (OR=6.16, CI:1.97-19.2). HCWs reporting stigma and discrimination had greater non-work concerns (OR=1.74, CI:1.09-2.79) and perceived impact (OR=4.57, CI:2.82-7.46). In conclusion, front-line HCWs, such as medical and nursing staff working in hospitals and health centres, reported higher work concerns compared to allied health professionals and support staff. The majority of HCWs experienced staff shortages, increased workload, and stress due to the demands of the pandemic. These findings highlight the need for targeted organisational and psychosocial support measures and increased awareness for frontline HCWs to improve their resilience during such health crises.
journal: Journal of Public Health and Development

title: Post-COVID-19 Three-year Trends of Clinical Profile and Outcome of Infants (1-12 months) Hospitalised at the Paediatric Department of a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital of Gujarat, Western India: A Retrospective Study
abstract: Introduction: The post-neonatal period (1-12 months) also represents a critical vulnerability window in child health. Despite substantial global progress in reducing under-five mortality, infant hospitalisations beyond the neonatal period continue to pose considerable challenges, particularly in developing countries where 10-15% of hospitalised infants succumb to preventable conditions. Understanding the clinical profile, temporal trends, and outcomes of hospitalised infants is essential for both, clinicians as well as administrators or policymakers. Aim: To study the 3-year trends of clinical profile and outcome of infants (beyond Neonatal Period) hospitalised at tertiary care teaching hospital after the end of the “Coronavirus Disease2019 (COVID-19) pandemic”. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study was conducted at the Department of Paediatrics, Shree Krishna Hospital, Pramukhswami Medical College, Karamsad, Gujarat, India over three years (July 2022 to June 2025). All consecutive indoor infants aged 1-12 months during the study period were included. The demographic details and clinical details including outcome were retrieved from medical records and pertinent information collected using a predesigned, structured proforma. Data were analysed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical methods. Results: A total of 177 infants were enrolled (Year-wise n=78, 76 and 23, respectively). The overall study cohort showed male predominance of 114 (64.4%). Respiratory infections emerged as the leading diagnosis in 60 (33.9%), followed by cardiovascular disorders 30 (16.9%). About 64 (36.2%) required Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) admission with critical illnesses. Successful discharge in 151 (85.3%) and mean±SD length of stay was 6.7±8.7 days. Significant relationship was found in trends for increasing prematurity (1.3% to 17.4%, p-value=0.002), declining immunisation completion (65.4% to 26.1%, p-value <0.001). Socio-economic status showed highly significant associations with both outcomes (p-value=0.003) and PICU admission (p-value <0.001). Conclusion: Post-COVID-19 epidemic, 3-year trends showed the temporal trends of rising prematurity rates, declining immunisation rates, and persistent high Discharge Against Medical Advice (DAMA) rates. This study provides essential baseline data for designing evidence-based interventions at tertiary care settings that serve vulnerable populations.
journal: Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research

title: Healthcare activity of an emergency ventilation unit in the emergency room during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic
abstract: Describir la actividad asistencial de una Unidad Ventilatoria de Urgencias (UVENURG) y analizar la tasa de fracasos y relación entre el fracaso de la ventilación mecánica no invasiva (VMNI) y distintos factores clínicos. Estudio observacional descriptivo retrospectivo de pacientes que iniciaron VMNI en la UVENURG del Hospital General Universitario Reina Sofía entre 08/03/2020-26/05/2021. Se recogieron variables demográficas, comorbilidad, datos clínicos y analíticos, etiología, modo ventilatorio y escala SOFA, definiendo el fracaso como escalada a ventilación invasiva (VMI) o éxitus. Se atendieron 8.040 pacientes; 384 (4,77 %) iniciaron VMNI. La edad media fue 77 años. El 50,5 % eran hombres, pluripatológicos, y el 29,2 % recibía oxigenoterapia domiciliaria. La frecuencia respiratoria media fue 27,3 rpm; la SpO2/FiO2, 322,5; el síntoma predominante fue la disnea (86,7 %), con RALE 0 en el 51 %. La insuficiencia cardiaca fue el diagnóstico más frecuente (51 %), seguido de agudización de EPOC (32 %) y de COVID-19 (15,4 %). Modos ventilatorios: bilevel 78,9 %, CPAP 7,3 % y mixto 13 %. El 22,1 % de los pacientes tuvo fracaso de la VMNI (4,5 % VMI y 20,3 % éxitus). Se asociaron al fracaso: varón, fiebre, COVID-19, oxigenoterapia previa y modo mixto. Hubo diferencias significativas en tensión arterial, frecuencia cardiaca y respiratoria, SpO2, proBNP, PCR, procalcitonina, pH, pCO2, lactato y SOFA. La creación de UVENURG durante la pandemia por COVID-19 no afectó a los resultados obtenidos al tratar patologías como el edema agudo de pulmón y la agudización del EPOC. La tasa de fracaso en pacientes afectos por COVID-19 es similar a otras series, y mayor que las anteriores patologías.
journal: Revista Española de Urgencias y Emergencias

title: Dexmedetomidine: A Promising Agent to Enhance Tolerance of Non-invasive Ventilation in COVID-19 Patients: A Narrative Review
abstract: COVID-19 patients can exhibit a hyperinflammatory response, which may result in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and hypoxemic respiratory failure. While the effectiveness of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) for treating COVID-19 patients with ARDS is not well established, many clinicians still opt for this treatment. Patient intolerance is the primary factor limiting the use of NIV, highlighting the need for sedative agents. Dexmedetomidine (Dex), an α2 adrenergic receptor agonist, is used as a sedative and anxiolytic medication. Unlike other sedatives, Dex does not act through the GABA pathway, so it does not depress the patient's respiratory drive. This drug also exhibits antioxidant effects and modulates the inflammatory system, making it potentially more appropriate for hyper-inflammatory states in COVID-19 patients. Despite the studies, our knowledge about the choice of sedative agents in this condition remains limited. This narrative review aims to provide information about the role of sedative agents, particularly Dex, in COVID-19 patients undergoing NIV. We conducted a literature search to examine the mechanisms of the human immune response to COVID-19, the immunomodulatory effects of Dex, and how this agent can enhance the acceptance of NIV among COVID-19 patients. The beneficial effect of Dex with antioxidant and immunomodulatory mechanisms has been shown in various studies. While there is a significant amount of research regarding the role of Dex in non-COVID patients undergoing NIV, studies focusing on COVID-19 patients are limited and primarily consist of case reports and retrospective observational studies. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that Dex may help improve the tolerability of NIV. Dex not only reduces agitation and delirium but also enhances the acceptance of NIV treatment. Due to its immunomodulatory and antioxidant effects, it can be considered a viable option for improving patients' respiratory status. However, future interventional studies are essential to understand better the efficacy and safety of Dex in severe COVID-19 patients.

title: Documentation Gap Analysis: Independent Audit of TGA COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Monitoring Plan
abstract: This independent audit evaluates the TGA COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Monitoring Plan (February 2021). The Plan operationalised National Cabinet's commitment to enhanced pharmacovigilance accompanying provisional approval, covering 68.4 million doses, 91.2% of Australia's rollout. Enhanced monitoring claims cannot be independently verified when the underlying processes are undocumented. This audit tests whether that verification is possible.The audit finds a systematic failure to demonstrate the enhanced monitoring underpinning Australia's largest provisional medicine rollout. Only 3 of 19 audited outputs (16%) are fully documented; 16 (84%) are partially or not documented. This is despite the TGA's own OAIC-directed searches surfacing 2,218+ pages of potentially relevant material in September 2024, none identified as Plan-implementation documentation. The TGA reports 148 signals investigated and 57 regulatory actions taken (the signal count was updated to 150 in the subsequent Question on Notice 559). No audit trail links signals to actions, and 91 signals have no documented disposition in the record. The OAIC found that the implementation records "cannot be found or do not exist".Senior TGA officials told the Senate (9 October 2025) that monitoring occurred through "day-to-day processes," without systematic tracking against Plan objectives. The TGA cannot demonstrate documented implementation of its own Safety Monitoring Plan. This is a potential failure of regulatory accountability for the largest provisional medicine rollout in Australia's history.The audit's open-source methodology applies ISO 19011:2018, ANAO guidance, and OSINT principles to public and FOI records, providing evidence for independent investigation and pharmacovigilance reform aligned with international standards and recognised good practice, including ICH E2E and CIOMS. It is published under CC BY 4.0: open access and independently replicable.The audit repository, containing the supporting evidence, primary sources, methodology, version history, and replication resources, is maintained at: https://github.com/paulrekaris/TGA-COVID19-Vaccine-Safety-Monitoring-AuditUpdated versions of this paper are available on SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6333058Version 6 note: This revision adds substantial documentary and regulatory analysis, including a new Appendix mapping the national enhanced-monitoring commitment, February 2021 Plan, provisional-registration framework, sponsor obligations and Commonwealth accountability requirements. It also updates FOI/OAIC, Senate and TGA evidence and refines regulatory framing, assessment scope and implementation-tracking analysis. Audit ratings and overall conclusions are unchanged.

title: Expression of concern—COVID-19: rapid antigen detection for SARS-CoV-2 by lateral flow assay: a national systematic evaluation of sensitivity and specificity for mass-testing
abstract: In June, 2021, eClinicalMedicine published the paper COVID-19: Rapid antigen detection for SARS-CoV-2 by lateral flow assay: A national systematic evaluation of sensitivity and specificity for mass-testing.1 Subsequently, the journal published a letter exchange between a reader and the authors.2,3 In this exchange, Deeks and colleagues questioned the accuracy and reporting of the lateral-flow test data, while Peto and colleagues maintained that the analyses were valid and the underlying PCR results to validate the lateral-flow tests supported their conclusions.

title: Contação de história e ensino remoto: desafios e possibilidades na formação de leitores durante a pandemia da covid-19 Storytelling and remote teaching: challenges and possibilities in reader training during the covid-19 pandemic
abstract: No presente artigo discutimos acerca dos impactos da pandemia da Covid-19 na formação de leitores por meio da contação de histórias durante o ensino remoto, com foco nos desafios e possibilidades encontrados por duas professoras do Ensino Fundamental – Anos Iniciais, de uma escola pública de Pau dos Ferros/RN. A pesquisa é de abordagem qualitativa, do tipo de campo e utiliza como técnica para a coleta de dados o questionário e a entrevista coletiva. Utiliza uma fundamentação teórica com base em autores como Alves (2020); Amarilha (2012); Busatto (2012; 2013); Bezerra (2020), dentre outros, que discorrem sobre as tecnologias e a contação de histórias, suas características e contribuições para o desenvolvimento do gosto pela leitura. Os resultados indicam que, apesar dos desafios, a contação de histórias e a mediação de leitura foram adaptadas criativamente para formar leitores, despertando seu prazer pelo universo fabuloso da literatura. Ademais, os dados apontam para a importância do papel do professor enquanto mediador, dado que durante o ensino remoto as professoras atuaram como facilitadoras do encontro dos alunos com as histórias através de diferentes técnicas e recursos digitais. Concluímos que, a partir das práticas de leitura desenvolvidas no contexto remoto, há a necessidade de investimento em novas políticas públicas que oportunizem um maior suporte e preparo técnico e humanizado para atender às demandas tecnológicas e pedagógicas que permeiam a docência.

title: Avaliação do impacto da pandemia de COVID-19 no transporte público por ônibus no município do Rio de Janeiro Assessment of the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on public bus transportation in the city of Rio de Janeiro
abstract: A pandemia de COVID-19 provocou mudanças no comportamento de viagens decorrentes das medidas de distanciamento social. Este estudo tem como objetivo avaliar os efeitos dessas mudanças na demanda do transporte público por ônibus no município do Rio de Janeiro. Utilizando dados públicos, foram aplicadas técnicas de modelagem de séries temporais e análise exploratória. A análise da série temporal do número de passageiros transportados evidenciou uma redução de 704 milhões de passageiros em comparação com valores previstos do cenário contrafactual sem a pandemia entre março de 2020 e dezembro de 2022. Além disso, observou-se um aumento contínuo da frota de veículos individuais nos últimos anos e uma redução de 8,4% na média mensal do fluxo de veículos depois da pandemia em comparação ao período anterior. Nos primeiros meses do período pandêmico, houve maior adoção do trabalho remoto. Esses resultados destacam alguns impactos nos perfis de deslocamento decorrentes da crise sanitária.

title: Challenges Faced by Cancer Patients and their Emotional Well-being During COVID-19 Pandemic: A Descriptive Cross-sectional Study from Central India
abstract: Background: Patients with cancer faced severe disruptions in healthcare access and heightened emotional distress during the COVID-19 pandemic. Thus, this study examined the challenges experienced by cancer patients in accessing treatment and the impact of the pandemic on their psychological well-being, including stress, anxiety, and depression. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using convenience sampling among 111 cancer patients admitted to the oncology units of a tertiary care center in central India. Data were collected through a well-validated and reliable structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, stress, anxiety, depression, and challenges faced during the pandemic. Data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY). Results: A high prevalence rate of moderate-to-severe stress (100%), anxiety (78.4%), and depression (64.9%) was reported among participants. The study identified several key challenges that affected patient care delivery during pandemics, including transportation issues, non-availability of telecommunication services, difficulty adhering to preventive measures, delays in surgery scheduling, and financial hardships due to lockdowns. Depression was significantly associated with transportation problems (p = 0.028) and surgery delays (p = 0.020), whereas anxiety was significantly associated with a lack of teleconsultation services (p = 0.014) and difficulty in maintaining preventive measures (p = 0.040). Conclusion: This study highlights the complex difficulties experienced by cancer patients during COVID-19, emphasizing the need for improved healthcare strategies, including digital health interventions, such as teleconsultation, remote monitoring, and virtual psychological support, to ensure uninterrupted cancer care during public health crises. Addressing these challenges can help mitigate the emotional burden on patients with cancer and improve overall treatment outcomes.

title: Thrombocytopenia and Other Hematological Features in COVID-19 Patients Referred to Shahid Mostafa Khomeini Hospital
abstract: Introduction: COVID-19 is a deadly virus, but there is still no appropriate cure for it. Hence, the target of this study was to estimate the clinical value of thrombocytopenia and other blood parameters in COVID-19 patients referred to Ilam Shahid Mostafa Khomeini Hospital from April and September 2020. Materials and Methods: In this cross-sectional study, patients with thrombocytopenia, associated with COVID-19, diagnosed at the Shahid Mostafa Khomeini Hospital in Ilam City during the spring and summer of 2020 were included. A checklist was used to record the hematological indicators of the patients. Further, an analysis of data using SPSS V20 software was performed. Results and Discussion: Overall, 66 thrombocytopenic patients were studied. Among patients who succumbed to the disease complications, 40 (67.8%) were male, and 19 (32.2%) were female. Mortality and survival rates were 90% and 10%, respectively. Conclusion: Due to the high mortality rate of COVID-19 patients with thrombocytopenia, platelet count can be considered a major risk factor, as well as a prognostic and diagnostic indicator in these patients.

title: The Therapeutic Effectiveness of Two Combined Regimens in Managing COVID-19 Pneumonia Patients: A Single-Center, Retrospective Observational Analysis
abstract: Introduction: Currently, there is no established pharmaceutical treatment for coronavirus patients; however, therapeutic approaches are still being developed to assess effective treatments during this unprecedented COVID-19 pandemic. Moreover, it has been observed that combination therapy may improve the individual’s treatment output. The present study aimed to compare the effectiveness of two independent combination regimens to improve the health conditions of individuals infected with a novel coronavirus. Methods: The current study was a retrospective, single-centered observational study. It included 100 COVID-19-positive patients with age ≥18 years, all with confirmed positive laboratory results. The patients’ clinical and laboratory data were recorded. The participants were classified into two distinct groups based on the therapeutic regimens: group I received regimen I, which included azithromycin, favipiravir, clopidogrel, and acetaminophen, and group II received regimen II, which included ceftriaxone, levofloxacin, methylprednisolone, clopidogrel, and acetaminophen. Results and Discussion: Patients following regimen II showed improvements in white blood cell count (WBC) (P = 0), lymphocyte cells (P Conclusion: This study indicated the beneficial effects of a 3-day short-term treatment with regimen II, which included ceftriaxone, levofloxacin, methylprednisolone, clopidogrel, and acetaminophen, compared to regimen I, which included azithromycin, favipiravir, clopidogrel, and acetaminophen, in patients. As there is insufficient evidence regarding the safety of these regimens, further investigations are needed to support additional research for the treatment of patients with COVID-19 pneumonia.

title: Revealing the Unseen: Post COVID-19 Biomarkers, Severity, and Outcome Mysteries
abstract: Background: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has passed, some patients still experience post-COVID-19 symptoms. It has been reported that COVID-19 symptoms can persist for more than three months after recovery. Objective: This study aims to analyze biomarkers, severity, and outcome factors associated with post-COVID-19 symptoms. Methods: This prospective cohort study involves hospitalised COVID-19 patients who were followed for up to 3 months after discharge. Clinical examinations and laboratory tests for MMP-9, TIMP-1, and IL-6 were conducted during hospitalisation and after three months. Results: We enrolled 76 COVID-19 patients, with a mortality rate of 30.26%. Among them, 55 individuals (30.91%) had no residual symptoms, 54.5% had acute COVID-19, 9.09% had ongoing COVID-19, and 5.45% had long-term COVID-19. title: Risk factors and clinical features associated with death at the COVID-19 isolation ward of Clairwood Hospital/KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa: A retrospective case-control study.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic posed significant challenges to healthcare systems worldwide. This study aimed to investigate the risk factors associated with death among patients admitted directly to the COVID-19 isolation ward at Clairwood Hospital. A case-control study was undertaken, involving a total of 400 study participants divided equally into 200 cases (deaths) and 200 controls (survivors). Data were collected retrospectively from medical records and analysed using Chi-square tests, univariate, and multivariate logistic regression. The patients had a mean age of 54.1 years (SD=18.9), with 217(54.2%) being female. A respiratory rate exceeding 20 breaths per minute was documented in 177 patients (44.2%), a heart rate greater than 100 beats per minute in 99 patients (24.7%), and a SpO2 level below 85% on room air in 79 patients (19.7%). Cough was the most common symptom, occurring in 239 (59.7%) patients, while hypertension was the most prevalent comorbidity, present in 157 (39.2%) patients at the time of admission. Chi-square test analyses demonstrated statistically significant associations between mortality and age, fever, cough, shortness of breath, hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease (CKD), obesity, respiratory rate, heart rate, and oxygen saturation (SpO2) (all p 60 years: 12.27 [95% CI: 1.27–118.44]), fever (aOR: 2.86 [95% CI: 1.29–6.31]), shortness of breath (aOR: 9.86 [95% CI: 5.64–17.24]), hypertension (aOR: 2.07 [95% CI: 1.05–4.11]), obesity (aOR: 4.68 [95% CI: 1.43–15.28]), were associated with increased odds of death among COVID-19 patients at admission. No statistically significant associations were observed for other variables after adjustment. Proactive measures to identify and manage these risk factors are crucial in reducing mortality rates and enhancing the overall care of COVID-19 patients in isolation wards.
journal: Journal of Public Health and Development

title: Use of IoT in Quarantined Hotels during COVID-19 and lessons learnt
abstract: This paper investigates how the Internet of Things has helped understand guest behaviour in a quarantined hotel during the COVID-19 pandemic by using WI-FI data analytics and AI CCTV cameras. Overall, it is indicated that A.I. technology which, would help hotels learn guest behaviours and in anticipating the needs of future guests, is inadequately used in the hotels industry.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Online Teaching Resources in Higher Education During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly disrupted traditional teaching and learning processes in higher education, necessitating the rapid adoption of online instructional delivery resources. This study evaluates the impact of online teaching resources on instructional delivery among tutors in Colleges of Education in Northern Ghana during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study employed a descriptive survey design, with data collected from 100 tutors selected through purposive sampling across ten Colleges of Education. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire administered and analyzed using descriptive statistics. The findings revealed that several online instructional resources were available to tutors during the pandemic, with Zoom (98%), Telegram (90%), Microsoft Teams (85%) and Google Classroom (60%) being the most commonly used platforms. Tutors utilized these resources primarily for delivering online lectures, sharing course materials, conducting e-assessments, providing feedback to students and completing course outlines during school closures. The results further indicated that the use of online teaching resources positively influenced instructional delivery by enhancing flexibility in teaching, improving tutors’ digital competencies, facilitating collaborative learning and ensuring the continuity of academic activities. The study concludes that online instructional delivery resources played a critical role in sustaining teaching and learning during the pandemic and recommends increased institutional support and continuous professional development for tutors to enhance effective integration of digital technologies in higher education

title: Pyramid Vision Transformer-based COVID-19 Detection Using Self-supervised Learning and Pretraining on Chest X-ray Images
abstract: Introduction: COVID-19 remains a public health emergency, necessitating rapid and accurate diagnostic techniques. Chest X-ray imaging is a low-cost, widely used technique for the detection of COVID-19, but its interpretation by humans is laborious and prone to errors. In this study, we propose an automated detection of COVID-19 on chest X-rays using a Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) model with self-supervised learning (SSL), pre-training, and attention map visualization. The proposed method has the potential to be more accurate, interpretable, and efficient and thus clinically suitable. Materials and Methods: In this study, the COVID-19 Chest X-Ray Database on Kaggle, which comprises 36,116 images classified as normal, viral pneumonia, and COVID-19, was employed. Largescale preprocessing operations, including the resizing, normalizing, and data augmentation operations, were carried out to generalize these models. Pretraining and fine-tuning the PVT model on the dataset included SSL, dropout regularization, and attention mechanisms. The primary metrics considered during the evaluation were the Measurement of Lung Severity Score (LSS), segmentation accuracy, Severity Detection Precision (SDP), Detection Sensitivity of Opacity (ODS), Time-to-Severity Detection (TSD), and focal AUC-ROC score. Results: Fine-tuning the PVT model significantly improved performance across multiple metrics. LSS increased from 15% (pretrained) to 17% (fine-tuned), while segmentation accuracy improved from 88% to 91%. Dropout regularization slightly reduced LSS to 16% but enhanced SDP (80% to 90%) and ODS (78% to 85%). TSD decreased from 4.5s (pretrained) to 3.8s (fine-tuned), improving detection speed. The focal AUC-ROC score improved from 0.92 to 0.95 with fine-tuning and dropout, while the Misclassification Visualization Score (MVS) increased from 0.85 to 0.91, reducing misclassification rates. Data augmentation further enhanced accuracy (88% to 94%), precision (85% to 91%), and recall (83% to 90%). Discussion: This study demonstrates the effectiveness of SSL pretraining, dropout regularization, and data augmentation in improving COVID-19 detection performance. The significant improvements in precision, recall, and robustness highlight the model's potential for clinical deployment. Attention map visualizations further enhance trust and interpretability by illustrating key lung regions that the model focuses on, ensuring transparency in decision-making. Conclusion: The PVT-based model, integrated with SSL, fine-tuning, and attention mechanisms, provides a robust, interpretable, and efficient solution for COVID-19 detection from chest X-ray images. The results validate its potential for real-world clinical use, offering improved diagnostic accuracy, reduced misclassification, and enhanced detection speed.

title: Comparison of Inhaled Epoprostenol and Inhaled Nitric Oxide for COVID-19 Induced ARDS in Critically Ill Adults: A Multicenter Observational Study
abstract: To compare the clinical impact of inhaled epoprostenol (iEPO) and inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) in mechanically ventilated patients with COVID-19 induced acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The primary outcome was the difference in the maximum change in PaO2:FiO2 during the initial 24 hours after study group initiation between iEPO and iNO. Secondary outcomes included differences in inpatient mortality and hospital length of stay. Multicenter, observational cohort study. Eleven hospitals in Arizona, Colorado, and Wyoming. Adult patients with a documented diagnosis of COVID-19 admitted between January 2020 and January 2022 who received continuous administration of inhaled epoprostenol (iEPO) or inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) and moderate to severe ARDS, defined as a partial pressure of oxygen to fraction of inspired oxygen (PaO2:FiO2) ratio of < 150 mmHg. None A total of 200 patients were enrolled in the study with equal distribution of patients in the iEPO and iNO groups. The maximum change in PaO2:FiO2 ratio within 24 hours from baseline in the iEPO and iNO groups was 40.7 ± 57.1 and 62.7 ± 74.0 mmHg, respectively (p = 0.0194). Inpatient mortality was higher in the iEPO group compared to the iNO group (91% vs 72%, p = 0.001). The mean length of stay was longer in the iNO group compared to the iEPO group (28.3 days vs 18 days, p = 0.0002). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that variables associated with increased mortality included use of iEPO (OR, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.113 to 0.645), norepinephrine dose (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.004 to 1.090), and use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (OR, 0.133, 95% CI, 0.028 to 0.636). In patients with moderate to severe COVID-19 induced ARDS, use of iNO was associated with greater improvements in PaO2:FiO2 ratio and lower inpatient mortality.

title: Was Covid‐19 a Game‐Changer? Inequality, Governance, and Urban Food Systems in Bengaluru, India
abstract: Game-changing crises have been explored as catalysts for transformative change towards sustainability. In this article, we examine the extent to which the Covid-19 pandemic acted as a game-changer, reshaping an urban food system in the Indian city of Bengaluru. Drawing on interview data with food system actors, we show that while Covid-19 generated a proliferation of adaptive initiatives and temporary shifts in practices, these were uneven and largely short-lived. Governance responses were biased with respect to classification of essential services, spatially differentiated enforcements, and institutional visibility. These responses systematically favoured organised, capitalised actors, while marginalising informal vendors and peri-urban producers. As a result, rather than catalysing longer-term transformation, the pandemic intensified existing inequalities and consolidated the position of dominant actors. We argue that game-changing crises did not inherently produce transformative change; instead, they acted as filters that revealed and deepened underlying power structures. Our findings highlight the need for justice-oriented urban food governance frameworks that can sustain alternative arrangements beyond moments of crisis.

title: Uneven Geographies of COVID‐19 III: Social Geographies of a Syndemic
abstract: ABSTRACT In this final of a three‐part series of review articles on the uneven geographies of COVID‐19, we zoom in on the social geographies of COVID's pandemic phase. We discuss research findings from across the globe that offer insights into the ways in which this phase was experienced by different populations and in various socio‐spatial contexts. Intersectionality provides an important lens to understand how pre‐COVID inequalities and injustices intersected with the COVID crisis. By mobilizing syndemics theory we highlight the interlocking of multiple burdens of disease and unjust social conditions turning the pandemic into a syndemic, where deprived populations experienced a much higher burden of disease and negative side‐effects from public health restrictions. Findings on the changing role of public space, borders, and mobility and immobility are discussed. This is followed by an analysis of research that has focused on migrants, refugees, gendered work and violence, women, youth and young people. The article concludes with a discussion of different interacting crises temporalities in relation to socio‐spatial unevenness. Avenues for further research and conceptual developments are suggested.

title: The Impact of Perception of Risk at International Airports and Carriers on Travel Decision at the Time of COVID-19 Pandemic - An Investigation From QAIA
abstract: Introduction: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Jordanian government implemented strict health and safety measures at Queen Alia International Airport to mitigate disease transmission and ensure safe air travel. These interventions significantly influenced passenger behavior, prompting an assessment of traveler experiences and satisfaction during the health crisis to understand future travel decisions and safety planning. Aims: This study aimed to control the spread of infectious diseases and offer safe flights. The government of Jordan has implemented various measures at its international airport during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Such measures had a significant impact on travel behavior. While many travelers’ decisions were affected by the pandemic, it became a priority to assess their experiences at international airports and onboard during the health crisis to predict their future decisions. Methods: The cross-sectional questionnaire was created through Google Forms and distributed to travelers through emails, social media channels, and official websites during the spread of COVID- 19. Questionnaires were distributed through a purposive sampling technique to flight travelers who departed from Queen Alia International Airport (QAIA) to different destinations. Finally, 61 responses were collected and analyzed through SPSS 23. Results: This study revealed that most respondents agreed it was easy to get information about available flights, fares, and new travel regulations and restrictions, with an arithmetic mean of 4.02. In addition, results showed that airport staff were wearing face masks all the time, with an arithmetic mean of 4.39. However, the waiting time at the airport was incredibly long. In addition, responses illustrated that the airplane cabin was thoroughly cleaned and sterilized with an arithmetic mean of 4.05, but the meals were neither wholesome nor properly packaged. Discussion: Risks perception at airport and onboard significantly influenced traveler behavior during the pandemic. Quality of services, safety protocols, and operational efficiency are crucial for restoring traveler confidence and preparing for future health crises. Conclusion: The results of this study may help plan air travel based on the various experiences and levels of satisfaction of passengers. With this knowledge, stakeholders, health agencies, international airports, and airlines might make better plans for their safety management during pandemics.

Results: This study revealed that most respondents agreed it was easy to get information about available flights, fares, and new travel regulations and restrictions, with an arithmetic mean of 4.02. In addition, results showed that airport staff were wearing face masks all the time, with an arithmetic mean of 4.39. However, the waiting time at the airport was incredibly long. In addition, responses illustrated that the airplane cabin was thoroughly cleaned and sterilized with an arithmetic mean of 4.05, but the meals were neither wholesome nor properly packaged. Discussion: Risks perception at airport and onboard significantly influenced traveler behavior during the pandemic. Quality of services, safety protocols, and operational efficiency are crucial for restoring traveler confidence and preparing for future health crises. Conclusion: The results of this study may help plan air travel based on the various experiences and levels of satisfaction of passengers. With this knowledge, stakeholders, health agencies, international airports, and airlines might make better plans for their safety management during pandemics.

title: Next-Gen COVID-19 Diagnosis: Integrating SegFormer, MaxViT, and Explainable AI for Advanced Lung CT Imaging
abstract: Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the critical role of medical imaging, particularly lung CT scans, for diagnosing and monitoring the disease. Despite the importance of CT in detecting COVID-19, challenges remain in achieving high accuracy and robustness in diverse clinical settings, especially with varying image quality and presentation. This study introduces a deep learning framework combining SegFormer for segmentation and MaxViT for classification, aimed at improving the accuracy of COVID-19 diagnosis from lung CT scans using four diverse datasets. Materials and Methods: This work utilized four publicly available CT scan datasets: SARS-COV2- CTScan (Brazil), COVID-CTset (Iran), MosMedData (Russia), and BIMCV-COVID19+ (Spain), totaling 77,050 CT images from over 2,100 patients. The datasets were processed through various preprocessing and augmentation techniques, including CLAHE, noise filtering, and 3D transformations. The model’s segmentation was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), while classification accuracy was measured using standard metrics like precision, recall, and F1-score. Results: The proposed model achieved an average DSC of 0.91 across the datasets, with classification accuracy reaching 95.2%, 92.5%, 93.4%, and 94.1% for each dataset, respectively. Precision for COVID-19 detection was 96.4% on the SARS-COV2-CTScan dataset, with corresponding recall and F1-scores of 94.8% and 95.6%. Cross-dataset evaluations maintained consistency with an overall accuracy of 95.0% and a DSC of 0.90. Key novel metrics like the COVID-19 Severity Grading Index (97%) and Temporal Progression Index (96%) demonstrated the clinical relevance of the model. Discussion: The model demonstrated exceptional generalization ability across diverse datasets and imaging conditions. Augmentation techniques, such as MixUp and CutMix, significantly improved model robustness, with a 14% reduction in Dice loss and a 7% improvement in classification accuracy for rare cases. The explainability of the model, through attention heatmaps and feature attribution, further enhanced its clinical applicability by providing transparency and aiding decision-making. Conclusion: This study presents a robust deep-learning framework for COVID-19 detection from lung CT scans, demonstrating high accuracy, reliability, and interpretability across multiple datasets. Despite strong performance, there is room for refinement, particularly in handling noisy or atypical cases. The model is poised for clinical deployment, providing an effective tool for automated COVID-19 diagnosis and monitoring, with the potential for further improvement in real-world applications.

title: Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) Associated with COVID-19-PIMS-grade 3: A Case Report
abstract: Background: In the face of the rise of COVID-19, the multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with COVID-19 has been reported, and an increase in MIS-C cases has been observed throughout the world. The majority of these cases were similar to Kawasaki disease concerning clinical presentation. Case Presentation: Despite similarities, MIS-C cases present clinical and laboratory differentiation, which makes it essential to portray similar cases worldwide to have a better consensus in the future. A 7-year-old male child visited the hospital with the chief complaints of fever associated with chills, rigors, and excessive myalgia for 3 days. He had a history of elevated high C-reactive protein (CRP) of 42.7 mg/L. He was diagnosed with Paediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome (PIMS)-grade 3. Here, for the first time, we bring an Indian MIS-C case with COVID-19-associated Paediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome (PIMS)-grade 3. Conclusion: PIMS-TS infection in paediatrics is associated with a wider range of complications, and the importance of musculoskeletal complications in PIMS-TS has been discussed.

title: Adaptive Solutions: An interdisciplinary Study of Human and Organizational Adaptation during the Covid-19 Pandemic.
abstract: This exploratory qualitative study examines how professionals and organizational leaders connected to the Brazilian pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors experienced and responded to adaptive challenges arising from organizational disruption during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study adopts an interdisciplinary perspective at the intersection of Business, Organizational Psychology, and Organizational Studies, conceptualizing adaptation as a process involving both organizational responses and changes in human behavior, relationships, expectations, and established ways of working.The study combines a focused literature review with six semi-structured interviews conducted between July and September 2022 with professionals working across pharmaceutical/medical affairs, commercial operations, human resources, marketing and sales, information technology, and Agile transformation. The analysis was organized around five interconnected domains: leadership, Agile management, Agile HR management, performance management, and knowledge management. Particular attention was given to the distinction between technical challenges, which can be addressed through existing expertise and established procedures, and adaptive challenges, which may require changes in behaviors, assumptions, relationships, and patterns of interaction.The findings indicate that organizational disruption exposed limitations that could not always be addressed through technological or procedural interventions alone. Participants described changes in work structures, stakeholder relationships, leadership practices, collaboration, prioritization, communication, and employee support. Agile practices were described as one mechanism for enabling shorter learning cycles, greater collaboration, distributed decision-making, and adaptation to changing stakeholder needs. At the same time, the interviews suggest that Agile practices were more meaningful when accompanied by attention to people, relationships, communication, leadership, and the capacity to reconsider established ways of working.The study contributes to interdisciplinary research on human and organizational adaptation by connecting external disruption with individual and collective responses within organizational settings. Rather than presenting Agile management as an independent solution, the findings suggest that adaptive capacity emerges through the interaction of human behavior, leadership, organizational practices, knowledge processes, and changing environmental demands. The study offers exploratory implications for organizational psychology, organizational behavior, leadership, human resource management, and organizational change research.Keywords: human adaptation; organizational adaptation; adaptive challenges; organizational change; organizational psychology; leadership; Agile management; knowledge work; pharmaceutical industry; COVID-19.

title: Patterns of Acute Liver Injury and Post‐Acute Liver Sequelae of COVID‐19
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) is known to cause acute liver injury (ALI) in COVID‐19 patients. This study explores the association between ALI patterns and the occurrence of long‐term hepatic complications in patients with and without existing chronic liver disease (CLD). Methods Within the Veterans Health Administration system, we identified patients testing positive for SARS‐CoV‐2. ALI was categorised based on injury type within the first 30 days post‐infection into hepatocellular, cholestatic, or mixed patterns. Cox regression was employed to analyse the link between ALI types and hepatic complications post‐acute COVID‐19 phase in patients with and without pre‐existing CLD. Results Of 173 111 COVID‐19 patients, 1843 (1.1%) suffered from ALI: 1542 hepatocellular, 180 cholestatic and 121 mixed. Among these, 51 291 (29.6%) had pre‐existing CLD. Post‐acute hepatic dysfunction was notably higher in ALI patients, with adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) of 2.19 for hepatocellular, 1.57 for cholestatic and 5.75 for mixed injuries. Patients with pre‐existing alcohol‐associated liver disease had a significantly increased risk of decompensation (aHR = 6.86), followed by those with Metabolic Dysfunction‐Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) (aHR = 1.56). Conclusions COVID‐19–associated ALI was associated with increased risk of post‐acute hepatic dysfunction and decompensation, with the highest risk observed among patients with a mixed hepatocellular‐cholestatic injury pattern. Among patients with pre‐existing CLD, ALD was most strongly associated with subsequent hepatic decompensation, while MASLD showed a more modest association.

title: Beneath the surface: Innate immune responses and brain pathology following SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Respiratory viruses such as influenza are known to affect the central nervous system (CNS), including disruption of the blood-brain barrier, neuroinflammation, and neuronal damage, and similar alterations have been described in postmortem brain tissue from severe COVID-19 patients. Chapter 2 reviews these findings, focusing on vascular changes, neuroinflammation, neuronal injury, and protein aggregation, alongside neuroimaging and biofluid studies in PASC patients suggesting that CNS alterations can persist beyond the acute phase. However, most existing evidence comes from severe or fatal cases, often involving underlying conditions, leaving the consequences of mild infection, their time course, and underlying mechanisms poorly understood. Non-human primate (NHP) models offer a valuable translational system to study SARS-CoV-2-induced immune activation and neuropathology longitudinally under controlled conditions. This thesis aimed to investigate the progression of SARS-CoV-2-associated neuropathology and protein alterations in blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) following mild infection, and to explore potential links with neurodegenerative disease processes. Chapter 3 examined neuroinflammation in NHPs following Delta variant infection. Longitudinal PET imaging targeting the 18 kDa translocator protein (TSPO) showed widespread increases in signal, indicating immune cell activation in the brain. This was confirmed postmortem by increased TSPO expression in endothelial cells, astrocytes, and microglia in the hippocampus and pons. This neuroinflammatory response persisted for several weeks, indicating sustained CNS effects beyond the initial infection. Chapter 4 investigated the substantia nigra at multiple timepoints, given that SARS-CoV-2 infection may increase vulnerability of the dopaminergic system. Findings showed loss of dopaminergic neurons and persistent innate immune activation in the substantia nigra during both post-acute and long-term phases. Neurofilament light chain (NfL), a marker of neuronal injury, was acutely elevated in blood and remained elevated in CSF at later timepoints similar to patterns reported in Parkinson's disease, severe COVID-19, and PASC. These results suggest overlap in pathological mechanisms between SARS-CoV-2 infection and Parkinson's disease-related neuropathology. Chapter 5 explored protein alterations in blood and CSF seven weeks post-infection using a sensitive CNS-focused proteomic panel, identifying changes in inflammation-, synaptic dysfunction-, and neurodegeneration-related proteins resembling profiles seen in neurodegenerative disorders. Amyloid-related proteins were relatively decreased in CSF, a pattern which is similarly observed in Alzheimer's disease, while NfL remained elevated. These protein changes were compared with gene expression data from cerebellum and hippocampus tissue, revealing consistent alterations across biological compartments and highlighting candidate CNS-associated pathways. Chapter 6 integrates these findings, showing that even mild SARS-CoV-2 infection can cause persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal damage, and protein alterations resembling neurodegenerative diseases. While it remains unclear whether SARS-CoV-2 initiates or exacerbates neuropathology, this work identifies shared virus-CNS mechanisms and underscores the need for translational models and longitudinal human studies to identify biomarkers of virus-associated neurological risk.

title: Affective and Physiological Associations of Teacher Emotional Exhaustion and Resilience During the COVID-19 Endemic
abstract: Abstract: Teachers have continued to report elevated emotional exhaustion well into the COVID-19 endemic phase, yet the physiological correlates of this exhaustion and of teacher resilience remain poorly understood. This study examined the biopsychosocial associations of teacher well-being during the COVID-19 endemic (May 2022). As educators ( n = 44 expatriate teachers in the United Arab Emirates; M age = 37.2 years, SD = 8.9; 68.2% female) returned to in-person instruction, they faced prolonged professional demands impacting both psychological health and physiological regulation. Using a multimethods quantitative design, this study investigated how levels of perceived emotional exhaustion (MBI Emotional Exhaustion subscale) and resilience (CD-RISC-10) were associated with affective balance during teaching (PANAS-SF) and objective biomarkers of stress. Physiological assessments included the cortisol awakening response (CAR; n = 38) to measure hypothalamic – pituitary – adrenal (HPA) axis activity and heart rate variability (HRV; n = 19–36 depending on parameter) to assess autonomic nervous system (ANS) regulation during resting, teaching, and recovery phases. Results indicated that higher levels of perceived emotional exhaustion were significantly associated with lower affective balance and increased total cortisol output (CAR AUCG), suggesting elevated tonal HPA-axis load. Conversely, higher perceived resilience was strongly associated with superior autonomic recovery following classroom instruction (HRV recovery) and a more positive affective balance. These findings suggest that perceived emotional exhaustion and resilience are anchored in divergent physiological pathways: chronic endocrine activation and dynamic autonomic flexibility, respectively. These distinct biopsychosocial associations highlight the importance of recovery-oriented interventions in educational settings. Practical implications focus on HRV biofeedback and systemic structural supports to enhance teachers' self-regulatory capacity and physiological rebound.
